source.title: From Weights to Features: SAE-Guided Activation Regularization for LLM Continual Learning
source.authors: Evan Ning; Wei Xue; Dong Lou; Yi-Ke Guo

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether SAE feature directions and neuron directions in an LLM show the representational separation and overlap predicted by superposition, extending the investigation to Gemma-2 9B-it rather than reproducing the original toy-model method.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own measurements of SAE-feature/neuron separability, neuron-to-feature mapping, and cross-task exposure under weight- versus feature-space protection. Continual-learning benchmark scores and hyperparameter sweeps are not rows: they evaluate the proposed method rather than directly measuring a claim version. The text's claims about SAE coverage and feature interpretability do not establish completeness or canonicality.
record.test_reason: Mainly a continual-learning method paper that assumes superposition. Its Section 5.1 analysis does measure, in Gemma-2 9B-it, how SAE features are spread across MLP neurons and whether neuron directions are task-selective. That bears on V4 (indirect evidence of features spread across neurons in LLMs) in a new setting. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that polysemanticity is a structural barrier to weight-space regularization in LLMs: Fisher-important neurons are not task-separable and weight protection is nearly non-selective, while SAE features give a more selective basis. They note that results are limited to Gemma-2 9B-it and that SAEs capture about 85–95% of activation variance.
record.recipe_differences: Measures SAE-feature and neuron-direction separability and collateral exposure in an LLM continual-learning setting; it does not reproduce the original toy-network feature-sparsity and geometry experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Task pair and benchmark affect separability and collateral exposure: TRACE and MedCL differ, and the reported per-layer TRACE AUCs vary by layer and task pair.

fits_no_version.finding: Protection in SAE feature space is more task-selective than weight-space protection: collateral/intended ratio 0.61 (MedCL) and 0.43 (TRACE), versus 0.96/0.91.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature bases provide more task-selective units for constraining LLM fine-tuning than neuron/weight bases.

record.problems: The claim-related geometry measurements are reported for Gemma-2 9B-it only. Table 3 and Table 4 give no uncertainty estimates or statistical tests. The neuron-to-feature count is a 500–1350 range without layer-specific values. The study does not test completeness or stability of SAE units, and its limitations state that SAEs capture approximately 85–95% of activation variance.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweeps, phase transition or geometry.
No test of importance-based capacity allocation.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
Only Gemma-2 9B-it with Gemma Scope 16k SAEs at layers 9/20/31. There is no SAE reconstruction or recovery test (85–95% variance figure is cited, not measured) and no other models.
SAE features are assumed monosemantic; completeness, stability and canonicality are not tested.
No comparison of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: Any 5% neuron set captures only about 7% of a typical feature's participation mass, versus a random-set floor of about 5%. This directly bears on features being spread across many neurons.
Per-layer and per-pair SAE separability on TRACE. Raw AUC ranges 0.57–0.89, and mean AUC rises from 0.67 at layer 9 to 0.75 at layer 31; cross-domain pairs are more separable.
missing.locator: Figure 4 and the paragraph after it, Section 5.1.1

record.verdict_notes: Superposition is assumed as motivation, and the analysis is built to explain EWC's failure, not to test superposition itself. The V4 evidence is indirect and uncontrolled. The neuron-vs-SAE comparison confounds basis with selection criterion (Fisher vs activation) and layer coverage. The neuron-to-feature count lacks a random baseline and a stated threshold. There is a single training seed, and no uncertainty is reported for Tables 3–4. r7 and r9 are method-selectivity results and should not carry V4 verdicts; the reader's limits_scope label on them is removed.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-count-versus-dimension sweep, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometry are tested.
The paper measures polysemanticity-related overlap, but does not test the proposed capacity allocation account that important features get dedicated dimensions while others share.
No alternative causes of polysemantic neurons are tested.
Evidence is limited to Gemma-2 9B-it and its tested SAE/neuron bases and tasks; no other LLMs or model families are tested.
The study uses SAE features and measures their task separability and selective protection, but does not establish that SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
The study treats SAE features as directions but does not compare one-dimensional features against multidimensional features.

relationships.condition: Gemma-2 9B-it, TRACE and MedCL, top-5% units, Gemma Scope 16k SAEs
relationships.reason: Fisher-important neuron directions are not task-separable (0.498/0.502; r2, r4), unlike SAE directions (0.882/0.866; r1, r3). Neuron subspaces expose other tasks' features at 0.91–0.96 of their own (r6, r8). Median neurons draw on 500–1350 SAE features (r5). All of this is indirect, with no baselines or uncertainty for r5.
relationships.display_finding: Neuron directions were not task-separable (0.498/0.502) while SAE directions were (0.882/0.866), and neuron subspaces exposed other tasks' features at 0.91–0.96 of their own. A median neuron drew on 500–1,350 SAE features, with no baselines or uncertainty given. All of this evidence is indirect.

relation.reason: Beyond using SAEs for regularization, the study measures neuron-feature entanglement, task separability, and cross-task feature exposure.

tranche.reason: Section 5.1 reports representation measurements bearing on V4 in the new setting of LLM continual learning.

source_check.notes: The source inconsistently describes separability coordinates: residual-stream decoder directions in Section 5.1.1 versus 16,384-dimensional feature space in Figure 4; it also lists only TRACE task names when describing pairs for both benchmarks. Decomposition thresholds and uncertainty for the checked measurements are unreported; the random-neuron reference concerns feature mass, not the collateral ratio.
